In a world where artificial intelligence opens up new horizons, our faith in its potential unveils a new outlook where, together, humans and machines build a new future filled with knowledge, inspiration, and incredible discoveries.

The development of a functional humanoid robot underpins an era of abundance and well-being where poverty will disappear, and people will be able to choose what they want to do.

We can imagine millions of bipedal robots doing more work than all human labour does today freeing people from the servitude of some repetitive and boring tasks that nobody likes to perform.

We believe that we have enough abundance to take care of everyone who is displaced. Eventually, providing a universal basic income will lead to the true evolution of our civilization.

Labor shortages loom, as the demands on our built environment rise. With the world’s workforce increasingly moving away from undesirable tasks, the manufacturing, construction, and logistics industries critical to our daily lives are left exposed.

By deploying our general-purpose humanoid robots in environments deemed hazardous or monotonous, we envision a future where human well-being is safeguarded while closing the gaps in critical global labour needs.

Name: University of Aberdeen Aerospace Society
Description:
Welcome to the University of Aberdeen Aerospace Society! 
We are a student run society excited in all things aerospace. If you are looking for a space to learn (without being graded), create things that hopefully fly, or just hang out, then we are the society for you! 

There is a lot of space for growth and creation here at AESOC. We have multiple ongoing student run and industry backed projects that allow our members to practice theory learned in class, pick up industry standards, and create freely. 

Fixed Wing UAV: The main project is our fixed wing UAV which is a huge undertaking and a huge thing - with a wingspan of over two meters. 

Quadcopter: Leaning onto the EEE/Computer Science side, we are developing a quadcopter from the ground up without using standard, off the shelf quadcopter components. The avionics and control systems will be programmed in house by us and we will use as few non-standard libraries as possible. 

Helical Antenna: Still on the drawing board, we are exploring the possibility of creating a helical antenna with the intention to track a weather satellite and get a live picture of the Earth as it passes over.  

Robotic Arm: In a joint venture between the Robotics and Aerospace societies, we are developing a robotic arm as a development platform to use for future projects. We may even try and get it to do the tracking for us on the helical antenna. 

When and Where
We meet weekly during the academic semester in Fraser Noble Teaching Lab 3 from 2:00-3:00 pm. Swing on by if you have any questions, want to check out what we're up to, or watch some frustrated students try engineering.

Name: Optimising Technologies
Description:
Optimising Technologies provides the legal roadmap, the on-robot safety software, and the liability insurance required to actually deploy it. Get your fleet out of the lab and into the real world

As autonomous robotic systems rapidly transition into real-world industrial environments, they hit a critical bottleneck: the liability gap. Following new regulations like the 2026 EU AI Act, autonomous systems are legally designated as "High-Risk." Traditional deterministic safety audits fundamentally fail to validate probabilistic AI behaviors. This leaves enterprise buyers facing massive boardroom liabilities, fleet groundings, and uninsurable operational risks.

OpTech bridges this engineering-to-insurance bottleneck. We provide an end-to-end continuous assurance lifecycle that translates complex machine physics into structured actuarial risk. Our proprietary three-tier architecture includes:

• NOMOS: A pre-market simulation gateway utilizing adversarial testing to compress legacy compliance queues from 18 months down to 12 weeks.

• SENTINEL: An on-robot, active runtime continuous protection firewall featuring a 10-second "black-box" safety telemetry logging engine to isolate liability.

• LEDGER: The industry’s first Robotic Managing General Agent (MGA), unlocking tier-1, Lloyd's-backed liability capacity based on live machine telemetry.

By deploying active safety firewalls across a scaling global fleet, OpTech is building an impregnable data moat—capturing the world’s most comprehensive database of physical AI failure profiles to monopolize autonomous risk pricing.

Backed by global venture capital, partnering with premier research institutions like the UK's Manufacturing Technology Centre (MTC), and actively shaping national policy, OpTech is the foundational infrastructure making the robotics boom legally and financially deployable.

We don't build the robots. We make them insurable, compliant, and open for business.

Name: NeuroRobotics Lab
Description:
The Neurorobotics group at Newcastle University works at the intersection of robotics/mechatronics and neuroscience. On the one hand, it uses robotic and mechatronic technologies to study how the human brain plans, controls and executes movements, as well as how it acquires new motor skills, from the early stage of its development to its maturity. On the other hand, it aims to exploit the knowledge acquired from a healthy brain for a human-centered design of robotic and mechatronic systems, to better assess and intervene on movement-related brain pathologies, such as stroke and Parkinson’s disease. These research activities are strongly interdisciplinary and benefit from the opportunity to work with neuroscientists, clinical neurophysiologists and developmental psychologists.
The  group is led by Prof. Domenico Formica and has expertise in robotics for applications in neuroscience, control of physical human-robot interaction, and experimental motor neuroscience. On these themes prof. Formica is coordinating the EU project CONBOTS (www.conbots.eu), which aims at designing and testing a new class of robots, the CONBOTS, which physically couple people to facilitate the learning of complex sensorimotor tasks.

Name: Geometric Mechanics and Mechatronics in Robotics (gm2R) Lab
Description:
The gm2R Lab (Geometric Mechanics and Mechatronics in Robotics) is based in Cardiff University’s School of Engineering and led by Dr Seyed Amir Tafrishi (Lecturer in Robotics and Autonomous Systems). We build the next generation of robots by combining geometric mechanics (how shape and contact geometry govern motion) with hands-on mechatronics (actuators, mechanisms, sensing, and control).

Our research focuses on robots that don’t just “move”—they adapt: rolling and contact-rich machines, shape-transforming (origami-inspired) platforms, and systems that exploit underactuation and compliance to do more with less actuation. We develop the full stack—from mechanism design to motion planning and control, including rolling-contact planning, dynamic/non-prehensile manipulation, and energy-based control for variable-impedance actuation. We work closely with industry and university partners across Europe and Japan, and we are open to new industrial and global academic collaborations in robotics, embodied intelligence, mechatronics, motion planning, and control.

Name: Klerix Labs
Description:
Klerix gives warehouse and factory robots an on-board AI brain — perception, reasoning, and safe control that adapts to a changing floor with no re-integration per SKU.

The physical economy is stuck between two bad options. Fixed automation (caged robots, PLC cells) is pinned to one part and one layout, so any line change means a slow, costly rebuild. Manual material handling is scarce, expensive, and turns over at roughly 60% a year. General-purpose robots exist — but the intelligence to run them reliably in production does not. Demos work. Real shifts break them.

Klerix is the embodied-AI runtime, simulation, and fleet-ops layer for autonomous machines. Engineers model a work cell as a high-fidelity digital twin, train the skill on synthetic data, validate it against safety evals, then deploy to the robot fleet with an independent safety monitor and a full, replayable action trace. Functional-safety posture (ISO 13849, IEC 61508) and per-fleet edge isolation are built in from day one.

Our bet is simple: embodied AI plus simulation plus an edge runtime beats both rigid automation and scarce labor for the physical work that runs the economy. We serve warehousing, manufacturing, 3PL and sortation, food and beverage, automotive, and ports — operators spending over $1M a year on manual labor or boxed in by inflexible automation.

Every deployment feeds a proprietary dataset of real-world interaction traces, so each new skill model improves on the last.

Name: Digital Concepts Engineering Ltd
Description:
Since 2017, Digital Concepts Engineering have been developing and deploying solutions directly related to the conversion of vehicles and platforms to remote control, and are regarded as global leaders in Uncrewed Vehicle technology. Using our own high reliability, low latency control system, MarionetteTM, we have successfully converted a range of legacy platforms, including Armoured Fighting Vehicles such as FV510 Warrior, the US HMMWV, assorted trucks, 4x4s, 6 and 8 wheeled platforms, bomb disposal robots and bespoke uncrewed vehicles. Once converted, these platforms can be driven manually by an operator, either from within the vehicle or remotely, or via an AI interface, allowing autonomous operations. 
MarionetteTM is essentially a toolbox of vehicle or payload interface modules, controlling the engine, transmission, steering, braking, and other vehicle functions along with a variety of payloads, from digital sensors to hydraulic manipulators. This allows extremely rapid vehicle conversions, down to around six weeks from vehicle arrival in our workshops. MarionetteTM can also be used to replace or upgrade obsolete control systems, extending the life of otherwise solid platforms, as demonstrated on the Wheelbarrow EOD robots.
Recent work has focused on reducing round-trip control system latency to levels that facilitate high speed teleoperation (100kph), developing a universal control interface that can be used by human or AI controller, and study and development of alternative communications (radio and Free Space Optics) specifically for control of UGVs, along with First Person View (FPV) control at high speeds.
DCE also design and manufacture our own range of UGVs. Called “X-Series” these platforms range from 300kg and come in many variants, including reconnaissance, carriage, and fully submersible “bottom crawlers”. They are powerful, reliable, and cost effective, and have been used in several defence, agriculture, and nuclear decommissioning roles.

Name: AIRA - Artificial Intelligence. Real Abilities

AIRA puts Robots to Work. We train Physical AI models on task specific data and deploy mobile, general-purpose Robots in real world manufacturing settings, supervising remotely, and supporting on site. We aim to solve the productivity challenge working directly with manufacturing customers, one task at a time.

Physical AI is not just about humanoids, it can be any AI system equipped with sensors and actuators: the sensors allow it to observe the world, and the actuators allow it to interact with and modify the world, covering several robotic form factors. It holds the promise of freeing human workers from physical tasks that are dangerous, laborious, or tedious. While several fields of AI have advanced significantly thanks to data and compute scaling in the recent decade, Physical AI only inches forward due to real world data scarcity and several other barriers. 

Unlike digital AI, where pre-training data can be scraped from the internet, Physical AI requires data from dynamic, real-world environments. This makes clean, deployment-specific, information-rich data the most important aspect of Physical AI training. AIRA’s mission is to accelerate the adoption of Robots in productive environments through a data-rich and scalable Physical AI Training Framework, granting robots Real Abilities and deploying them in real-world applications.

We want everyone to feel supported, and in doing so we welcome and celebrate diversity in backgrounds, including but not limited to, gender, sexuality, neurotype, ethnicity, class, age, and ability. Many in our community exist in an intersection of diverse groups and we understand that privilege takes many forms and is often not able to be compared across groups.
We host events and hold spaces for particular groups, such as women or neurodiverse people, in order to address issues which affect specific sets of people. All are welcome to attend such events with a respectful and open mind.

We welcome the membership and participation of those who have traditionally been positioned as privileged within the robotics community, in an effort to share experiences and work together to make the world of robotics a more inclusive space.
